title: Rollout config schema + migrations for Hosted canary rollouts (control plane)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
- We’re shipping GA “Hosted canary rollout workflow” (Console + orchestration + routing enforcement). This ticket is strictly the control plane config model and DB migrations needed to represent rollouts, steps, state, and the applied traffic split on Hosted routes.
- This needs to be: (a) additive + safe to roll back, (b) compatible with future Dedicated/Private parity, and (c) stable enough for audit timeline + cohort metrics tagging.

Goals
1) Define and land schema for:
   - Rollout object (identity + route binding + baseline/canary targets)
   - Step plan (schedule) + current execution pointer
   - Status/state model (draft/active/paused/completed/rolled_back/failed)
   - “Applied split” view needed by data plane (fast read path)
2) Provide migrations (DDL + backfill if needed) with rollback plan.
3) Backward compatibility strategy:
   - Routes without rollouts behave exactly as today
   - Data plane + Console can safely ignore unknown fields (for staged deploys)

Non-goals
- Orchestrator logic/state machine implementation (ENG-9140)
- Traffic splitting enforcement details in the data plane (ENG-9123)
- Policy evaluation rules (ENG-9146)

Proposed data model (Control Plane / ConfigDB)
Note: naming here is intended to map to current Config Service conventions (tenant-scoped, immutable revisions where possible, and explicit “current effective config” pointers).

A) New table: hosted_route_rollouts
Purpose: canonical rollout record, user-visible identity, and link to targets.

Fields (v0)
- rollout_id (uuid, pk)
- tenant_id (uuid, indexed)
- route_id (uuid, indexed)  // Hosted route
- display_name (text, nullable)
- description (text, nullable)
- created_at (timestamptz)
- created_by_actor_id (uuid)
- updated_at (timestamptz)
- updated_by_actor_id (uuid)

Target selection (baseline vs canary)
- baseline_target_type (text) // "route_revision" | "model_version" (v0: route_revision)
- baseline_route_revision_id (uuid) // existing route config revision
- canary_target_type (text) // same enum
- canary_route_revision_id (uuid)

Execution pointers (kept minimal; orchestrator owns transition logic)
- status (text) // "DRAFT" | "SCHEDULED" | "RUNNING" | "PAUSED" | "COMPLETED" | "ROLLED_BACK" | "CANCELED" | "FAILED"
- current_step_index (int, nullable)
- started_at (timestamptz, nullable)
- completed_at (timestamptz, nullable)
- last_error_code (text, nullable)
- last_error_message (text, nullable)

Guardrail / policy linkage (evaluated elsewhere)
- policy_bundle_version (text, nullable)  // for auditability, not enforcement
- guardrail_profile_id (uuid, nullable)  // reference to stored policy params if/when we persist them

B) New table: hosted_route_rollout_steps
Purpose: step plan + step execution timestamps. Orchestrator updates state per step.

Fields (v0)
- rollout_id (uuid, fk -> hosted_route_rollouts.rollout_id, indexed)
- step_index (int, indexed) // 0..N-1
- canary_traffic_percent (int) // 0..100
- min_soak_seconds (int) // 0 allowed for testing; Console will usually enforce >= 300
- requires_approval (boolean)
- step_state (text) // "PENDING" | "ACTIVE" | "PAUSED" | "SUCCEEDED" | "FAILED" | "SKIPPED"
- activated_at (timestamptz, nullable)
- deactivated_at (timestamptz, nullable)
- approved_at (timestamptz, nullable)
- approved_by_actor_id (uuid, nullable)

Stop conditions (reference only; evaluation lives in telemetry/orchestrator)
- stop_condition_profile_id (uuid, nullable)

Constraints
- PK: (rollout_id, step_index)
- Check: canary_traffic_percent between 0 and 100

C) New table: hosted_route_effective_split
Purpose: optimized read model for data plane. Keeps “what split should I apply right now for route X” without joining steps/rollout records.

Fields (v0)
- tenant_id (uuid)
- route_id (uuid)
- rollout_id (uuid, nullable) // null if no active rollout
- baseline_route_revision_id (uuid, nullable)
- canary_route_revision_id (uuid, nullable)
- canary_traffic_percent (int, not null default 0)
- split_state (text) // "NONE" | "ACTIVE" | "PAUSED" | "ROLLED_BACK" | "COMPLETED"
- updated_at (timestamptz)

Constraints
- PK: (tenant_id, route_id)
- Check: canary_traffic_percent between 0 and 100

Behavioral contract
- When no rollout is active: split_state=NONE, canary_traffic_percent=0, rollout_id=null.
- When a rollout is RUNNING: split_state=ACTIVE and percent reflects the current step.
- When paused: split_state=PAUSED and percent stays at last applied value (data plane continues to enforce; orchestrator does not advance).
- On rollback: split_state=ROLLED_BACK and percent set to 0 (baseline gets 100%).
- On completion: split_state=COMPLETED and percent may remain 100 until the route is updated/pinned (Console will typically promote canary to baseline and then clear the split).

Why a read model table?
- Data plane needs a stable, low-latency lookup keyed by (tenant_id, route_id), not an N-way join or status inference.
- It also makes it easier to implement kill switch / emergency reset by writing a single row per route.

Backwards compatibility / staged deploy plan
Phase 0 (safe deploy)
- Ship DB migrations adding new tables only. No changes to existing route config schema.

Phase 1 (write behind flag)
- Orchestrator (ENG-9140) writes hosted_route_rollouts + hosted_route_rollout_steps.
- Orchestrator is the only writer for hosted_route_effective_split (single source of truth).
- All writes gated by per-tenant feature flag (ENG-9180), so we don’t create partial data for non-enabled tenants.

Phase 2 (data plane read)
- Data plane (ENG-9123) reads hosted_route_effective_split. If row missing => treat as NONE.
- Important: treat unknown split_state values as NONE (defensive), and clamp percent to [0,100].

Phase 3 (Console read)
- Console reads rollout + steps for timeline. Console should not depend on effective_split for UI correctness (it’s an optimization/read model).

Rollback strategy
- Rolling back application code is safe because migrations are additive.
- If we need to hard-disable behavior in production, we can:
  (a) flip feature flag off (stops orchestrator writes + UI exposure)
  (b) set hosted_route_effective_split.canary_traffic_percent=0 for impacted routes (manual mitigation; should be codified in runbook)

Migration details
DDL
- Create tables hosted_route_rollouts, hosted_route_rollout_steps, hosted_route_effective_split.
- Indexes:
  - hosted_route_rollouts(tenant_id, route_id)
  - hosted_route_rollout_steps(rollout_id)
  - hosted_route_effective_split(tenant_id, route_id) as PK

Data migration / backfill
- None required initially.
- Optional follow-up: if we add a “route has active rollout” field, it should be derived from effective_split rather than duplicated.

Open questions
1) Do we need region-level splits in schema (e.g., canary 5% in us-east, 0% elsewhere)?
   - Current plan: no; split is per route, applied uniformly across regions. Any region-specific behavior handled in routing policy layer and out of scope for GA.
2) Do we need to persist deterministic cohorting hash inputs in control plane (e.g., hash_key enum)?
   - Recommendation: store only a “cohorting_mode” string on the rollout for auditability. Actual hash key inputs are in ADR and implemented in data plane. (If we do store, keep it optional and default to "TENANT_ROUTE_REQUEST" as per ADR.)
3) Promotion semantics at 100%:
   - At 100% canary, do we auto-promote canary route revision to become the route’s pinned revision?
   - For GA we likely require explicit user action in Console (“Promote”) or orchestrator finalization step. Schema supports both, but we should confirm with PM (Marissa) to avoid ambiguous COMPLETED state.

Acceptance criteria
- Migrations land in main with zero downtime approach.
- Orchestrator can create rollout + steps and update status and current step.
- A single-row read path exists for data plane to enforce split with no joins (effective_split).
- No behavior change for tenants without feature flag.
- Documented rollback playbook (how to zero split + clear rollout pointer).

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-canary-rollout-ga-prd.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/hosted-canary-rollout-workflow-design-spec.json
- ADR cohorting: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting.json
- Related: ENG-9123 (data plane enforcement), ENG-9140 (orchestrator APIs), ENG-9146 (policy engine guardrails), ENG-9152 (telemetry tags)

Implementation checklist
- [ ] Add migrations + verify on staging with production-like DB size
- [ ] Add Config Service models + DAO layer for v0 schema
- [ ] Add orchestrator write helpers for effective_split updates (atomic update per route)
- [ ] Add integration test: create rollout -> step to 1% -> effective_split reflects 1%
- [ ] Add docs snippet for on-call: manual reset of effective_split to 0%
comments: 2025-02-05 (Ethan Park): Kicking this off as a GA blocker. We need an additive schema + a simple read model for the data plane. Please bias toward “boring” relational tables over embedding step arrays in a single JSONB blob — we’ll need to query + index steps for timeline + audit and we want predictable migrations.

2025-02-11 (Mina Haddad): +1 on read model table. Data plane wants a single lookup keyed on (tenant_id, route_id). Also please ensure percent is int and clamped; we saw some float configs in older internal experiments that caused rounding weirdness.

2025-02-14 (Jordan Lee): For policy guardrails we’ll want to know: requested next percent, last step percent, and soak time. Storing min_soak_seconds + requires_approval per step is sufficient; enforcement will happen in policy engine at action time.

2025-02-18 (Chloe Martin): Console backend needs stable IDs and timestamps for the rollout timeline. Please include actor IDs on create/approve and track activated/deactivated timestamps per step. Even if orchestrator is the writer, having the schema now will unblock UI contract work (PR-28863).

2025-02-26 (Michael Nguyen): Drafted DDL locally. Question: do we want to model baseline/canary as “route_revision_id only” for v0? I kept target_type fields so we can expand to model_version later without rewriting tables. Minor overhead but buys forward compatibility.

2025-03-04 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure rollback plan is explicit. During beta we had a split mismatch incident and the fastest mitigation was “force 0% canary”. Having that as a single write to effective_split is good; we’ll want it in the runbook with exact SQL and safeguards.

2025-03-12 (Ethan Park): Agree with keeping target_type even if v0 is route_revision. This is one of those places where a tiny amount of schema flexibility avoids a migration under duress later. Proceed.

2025-03-20 (Michael Nguyen): Migrations are ready in a branch; waiting on final review re: COMPLETED semantics (whether effective_split stays at 100% or is cleared). I defaulted to keeping 100% until explicit promotion/clear to avoid surprise traffic changes.
